key_insight: Controlling presentation bias improves answer selection, while injecting majority pressure exposes decision instability as a reliability signal.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers test-time aggregation for heterogeneous LLM agents without validation data or prior knowledge of relative model strength.
method: Present one style-normalized reasoning trace per distinct answer.
Place each aggregating agent’s initially selected answer in the minority to probe decision instability.
Use bias-controlled selection and instability signals to aggregate answers.
evidence_signal: Across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and four heterogeneous LLM combinations, the framework reports higher average accuracy and better token efficiency than competing non-oracle aggregators, plus accuracy gains for multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to mathematical reasoning; style normalization must preserve substantive reasoning to avoid distorting answer quality.
paper_title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
